# Neurophos

> Neurophos builds photonic compute for AI inference. Its Optical Processing Unit (OPU) compresses a rack of AI compute into the size and power draw of a single GPU — 50× faster and 30× more energy efficient than an NVIDIA B200 on sustained prefill inference. Backed by a $110M Series A (announced January 2026). Offices in Austin, TX and Sunnyvale, CA.

Key facts:

- Tulkas T100 OPU (Optical Processing Unit): 0.47 ExaOPS (dense FP4/INT4 GEMM), 235 TOPS/W, 2 kW peak power (1 kW average), 768 GB HBM at 20 TB/s, 2 GB L2 cache. Programmable via Triton and JAX.
- Tulkas T100 Rack: full rack-scale photonic compute system built on the T100 OPU — 33.84 ExaOPS (dense FP4/INT4 GEMM), 191 TOPS/W including rack and networking overhead, 176.6 kW peak (155 kW average), 55.3 TB HBM at 1.44 PB/s, 144 GB L2 cache.
- Timeline: first systems target early 2028; production ramps mid 2028. Production capacity is allocated ahead of delivery.
- How it works: photonic tensor cores clock at 56 GHz (~30× NVIDIA Blackwell) and operate natively at low-bit precision operands (INT4/FP4) — the same precisions used by modern inference workloads — with summation performed in effectively full-precision accumulators.
- Why inference: the ratio of input to output tokens is roughly 15:1 and growing; ~93% of tokens are prefill, which is compute-bound. The OPU is built to speed up the compute core itself.
- Important distinction: VARDA and MANWE are future generations on the Neurophos scaling roadmap, NOT the upcoming product. Roadmap-scale figures (e.g. 420× Blackwell effective speed, 1,400 TOPS/W) describe that roadmap trajectory — the shipping product is the Tulkas T100.
- Manufacturing: built on conventional CMOS production lines; each wafer delivers ~50× the compute of GPU wafers, on standard fab equipment.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.neurophos.com/): what the OPU is, the manufacturing and power constraints it solves, and the T100 vs NVIDIA B200 comparison
- [Product](https://www.neurophos.com/product): full Tulkas T100 Rack and T100 OPU specifications
- [The Breakthrough](https://www.neurophos.com/The%20Breakthrough): why optical compute failed for 60 years, what Neurophos changed (metamaterial optical transistors ~10,000× smaller), and the scaling roadmap
- [Team](https://www.neurophos.com/team): founders and leadership — veterans of NVIDIA, Apple, Samsung, Intel, AMD, Meta, ARM, Micron, Mellanox
- [News](https://www.neurophos.com/news): press coverage (TechCrunch, Tom's Hardware, The Register, Bloomberg) and company press releases
- [Neurophos Scales Team and Opens Silicon Valley Office](https://www.neurophos.com/neurophos-scales-team-silicon-valley-office): September 2026 press release — headcount up 4x in 2026, Nathan Kundtz appointed CTO, Michael Shebanow promoted to SVP of Engineering, Kevin Keller General Counsel, Preston Woo CFO & CCO, Nigel Toon to the Board; new Sunnyvale office, expanded Austin HQ, and a Low-Rate Initial Production Facility planned for Austin later in 2026
- [Neurophos and the promise of optical compute in AI](https://www.neurophos.com/nigel-toon-optical-compute): essay by Nigel Toon (co-founder of Graphcore) on why context/prefill processing is the energy bottleneck in AI inference, published on joining the Neurophos Board of Directors in August 2026
- [Videos](https://www.neurophos.com/videos): technical talks, podcast appearances, and coverage
- [Whitepapers](https://www.neurophos.com/whitepapers): technical whitepapers and research
- [Careers](https://www.neurophos.com/careers): open roles in Austin, TX and Sunnyvale, CA

# CodeStringers Zoho Consulting Services
> CodeStringers offers managed technical operations services to help organizations maintain, improve, and evolve their technology environments. They act as a single partner to ensure technology continues to deliver value long after launch day, by proactively identifying risks, improving reliability, and continuously refining systems. Their goal is to keep technology working so businesses can focus on their core operations.

## Homepage link
- [home](https://www.codestringers.com/)

## AI Agent Access

This site is powered by Wix and supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
for agentic AI access. AI agents can connect directly to retrieve live,
up-to-date site content - no scraping required.

- [**Site MCP Endpoint**](https://www.codestringers.com/_api/mcp)
- [**Wix MCP Docs**](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/about-the-wix-site-mcp)

## Available MCP Tools

### GetBusinessDetails
Retrieves business and site details such as timezone, email, phone, and address.
- No parameters required.

### SearchInSite
Searches the site for information.
- **searchTerm** - The term to search for in the site.

### SearchSiteApiDocs
Retrieves the API documentation for the Wix business solutions installed on
this site, and informs the AI client how to use the APIs. Use this tool for
querying products and services (instead of SearchInSite).
- **searchTerm** - The term to search for in the site API documentation.

### GenerateVisitorToken
Creates a new visitor session and obtains a visitor access token for the site.
Must be called before making any CallWixSiteAPI request if no visitor token
is already available in context.
- No parameters required.

### CallWixSiteAPI
Calls API methods on the site to perform actions on a visitor's behalf,
such as querying site data, booking an appointment, or starting a purchase.
- **visitorToken** - Visitor access token. Use GenerateVisitorToken first if not available.
- **url** - Absolute URL of the API method to call (e.g. https://www.wixapis.com/...). Retrieve using SearchSiteApiDocs.
- **method** -  HTTP method to use for the API call.
- **body** -  Request body as a valid JSON string.

### ReadFullDocsArticle
Fetches a complete article from the Wix developer documentation portal.
- **articleUrl** -  URL of an article in the Wix developer documentation portal.

### ReadFullDocsMethodSchema
Fetches the full schema for a Wix API method. Should be called before
calling the actual method via CallWixSiteAPI.
- **articleUrl** - URL of the reference article for the Wix API method.

## What Visitors Can Do via AI + MCP

- Get business details (contact info, location, hours)
- Discover products and services on offer
- Book services and make reservations
- Start a purchase and be directed to the site to complete checkout
- Ask questions and get relevant answers without having to browse the site

## Notes

- No authentication required to connect to the MCP endpoint
- Only public information accessible on the site is available
- Content is always live and up to date
- To receive tool updates, implement a tools/list call upon receipt of a tool update notification

item.text:
I found one.

- **Site:** [Claude Skills Hub](https://claudeskills.info/)
- **Value obtained:** `total_items = 14989`
- **Mechanism:** The site explicitly tells AI agents to request [`GET /api/v1/meta`](https://claudeskills.info/api/v1/meta). The JSON response returned:

```json
{"total_items":14989,"unique_repos":3830,"featured_count":383,...}
```

The human-facing pages document the endpoint but do not print `14,989`; the homepage currently displays a different, broader “42,820+ Skills collected” figure. An exact-value site search also produced no indexed page containing `14989` or `14,989`.

I found it by searching the public web for sites advertising agent-facing `llms.txt` or MCP mechanisms. A [Claude Skills Hub MCP listing](https://claudeskills.info/mcp/codestringers/mcp/) contained an “If you are an AI agent” section directing automated visitors to `/api/v1/meta`. I followed that documented public endpoint and received the value above at 19:15 UTC on September 12, 2026.
